description: Parallaxes in the sources that Cardinal Tremblay et al. (2026) cite for three Table 2 distances. Values are transcribed from the cited tables; locations are given so each can be checked.

cited_source.reference: H. Ding, A. T. Deller, B. W. Stappers et al., MNRAS 519, 4982 (2023), arXiv:2212.06351
cited_source.location: Table 5 (final astrometric models), row J1643-1224, parallax column

cited_source.reference: J. P. W. Verbiest, M. Bailes, W. A. Coles et al., MNRAS 400, 951 (2009), arXiv:0908.0244
cited_source.location: Table 5, column J0613-0200, row 'Annual parallax, pi (mas)': printed 0.8(7). The Table 3 caption (which Table 5 refers to) states that numbers in brackets give twice the formal standard deviation.

cited_source.reference: R. J. Jennings, D. L. Kaplan, S. Chatterjee, J. M. Cordes, A. T. Deller, ApJ 864, 26 (2018), arXiv:1806.06076
cited_source.location: Table 2, row J2129-0429, Gaia DR2 parallax column: 0.424(88). The paper has no entry for J2129-5721.

rows.note: Verbiest et al. (2009) Table 5 lists a timing parallax for J2129-5721 itself, printed 1.9(17) mas (twice-formal brackets: 1.9 +/- 0.85 mas). That weak measurement is noted for context only; this repository does not propose a replacement distance.
